help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Guides and reference for publishing and running your applications.
help.dev.socket.q: How does my application receive requests?
help.dev.socket.a: Through a Unix socket, not a TCP port. The path arrives in the SELYNT_SOCKET environment variable — your application must listen on it. The panel only reports the application as up once it can connect to that socket, and stops the process if it never appears.
help.dev.env.q: How do I set environment variables?
help.dev.env.a: Create a .env file in the application folder, one variable per line as KEY=value. It is read on every start. The file is preserved when you remove the application without deleting its files.
help.dev.port.q: Can I open a TCP port?
help.dev.port.a: Not one reachable from outside: the application is stopped with the network_port_forbidden error. External access comes from the web server, which forwards to your Unix socket — that is what lets many applications share one server without port conflicts. Listening on 127.0.0.1 is allowed, so an application can talk to itself (a local cache, communication between workers).
help.admin.subtitle: Installation and operation guides for the plugin on this server.
help.admin.permissions.q: The panel returns a permission error
help.admin.permissions.a: Almost always the binary lost its setuid bit. Check with ls -l bin/core-selynt — it should read -rwsr-xr-x root root. Reinstalling through the Plugin Manager fixes it; the installer warns when it cannot apply it.
help.admin.notstarting.q: A customer's applications will not start
help.admin.notstarting.a: Check the application's STDERR on its page. Common causes: the application never creates its Unix socket, it tries to open a TCP port, or the chosen runtime no longer exists on the server. A socket_stuck error means the process started but never became ready.
help.admin.diagnostic.a: Yes, under the Diagnostic tab. It checks templates, vhosts, permissions, sockets, ACLs and logs, and points out what is out of place.

settings.isolation.title: Isolation between applications
settings.isolation.desc: With isolation on, each application runs without seeing the others — neither their files nor their processes. Useful when applications from different sources share one account. Off, they share the environment, as hosting normally works.
